implementation_decisions: Use a Linux anonymous O_TMPFILE opened relative to the already anchored destination parent, instead of a mutable staging filename. Unsupported host/filesystem behavior fails before publication; no permissive fallback or permission changes.
Flush/fsync and hash/count the held staging FD against the expected decoded raw authority after all source/member/manifest/directory input contexts have completed successfully.

Publish that exact held inode through Linux /proc/self/fd with os.link, dst_dir_fd and follow_symlinks=True. This is exclusive and cannot substitute a mutable staging pathname or overwrite an existing destination.

The successful exclusive hardlink is the publication point. Never unlink a published destination during later failure cleanup: another writer can replace it or modify its contents, and a stat-then-unlink guard cannot atomically establish continued pathname ownership.

Continue checking the actual named destination's expected full SHA/size and held-FD occurrence, parent identity and durability before returning successful verification. Any mismatch still raises and is not admitted.

All failures before publication leave no new destination, including all original archive/source refusals; a corrected archive may retry the same still-absent target. On an externally changed post-publication destination, verification rejects but retains the current destination untouched rather than deleting another writer's data. This distinction is explicit in documentation and current controls, not presented as universal no-output-after-any-error.

Closing an unpublished anonymous staging FD removes only invocation-owned temporary storage. There is no staging pathname or public-target rollback to race with another writer. Remove obsolete named-staging/rollback fields, imports and incidental controls; migrate actual callers, retain historical003 producers unchanged.
